messages:
Anya: Heads-up — hitting a pretty consistent bug in the Python SDK async codepath for tool/function calling + structured output. When I request a dataclass return type the result arrives as a JSON string instead of being deserialized to the dataclass. Minimal repro below.

Anya: ```py
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class User:
    name: str
    id: int

async def go(client):
    resp = await client.tool_call(
        "get_user",
        input={"user_id": 123},
        return_type=User,
    )
    print(type(resp), resp)  # EXPECT: <class 'User'> but see <class 'str'>
```

Matt: Which SDK version + python runtime? Is this only in async client or also sync?

Anya: py-sdk 0.9.4, python 3.11. Happening only on the async client (client.async or client in an async context). Sync client returns dataclass correctly.

Sasha: Curious — are you using streaming or full response? Could be double-jsonifying if the async path sets as_text somewhere.

Anya: Not streaming. Plain tool_call awaiting the response. No custom hooks.

Jin: I can reproduce locally. Quick dump of what I see: the network payload is correct (JSON object) but the SDK layer that maps to return_type gets a string. Looks like _deserialize is called twice in the async path so we end up with json.dumps(json_obj) -> string. Stack trace: ```
File ".../redwood/client/async_tooling.py", line 214, in _handle_response
  body = await resp.json()
File ".../redwood/serializers.py", line 89, in _deserialize
  return return_type(**json.loads(body))  # fails if body already a dict or already dumped string
```

Rowan: This rings a bell — we changed the async HTTP client wrapper in the release that added keep-alive pooling (commit a1b2c3d). Tests only covered sync path. I think the wrapper now returns str in some cases. PR that touched it: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/4321

ci-bot: CI failing: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/py-sdk-async/5678 — failing test: tests/test_toolcall_async_structured.py::test_dataclass_return

Matt: Assigning this to @Jin to triage & patch. Please add a regression test (sync + async), include a small changelog blurb, and add a short sample to the docs (devex/async_toolcall.md) so onboarding isn't blocked. :+1:

Jin: Got it. I'll push a reproducing unit test and a fix (looking at not calling json.dumps twice and making deserializer accept both dict and str). Targeting a small patch/PR by EOD tomorrow.

Anya: Thanks. Also flagging UX impact — a customer hit this during onboarding and it blocked their sample app. If possible add a quick sample app snippet to the docs that shows proper async usage with dataclasses.

Rowan: One more note — we should also check toolcall when return_type is pydantic BaseModel (same code path) and for function-calling where the tool returns a JSON-encoded string intentionally. Need to preserve that case.

Jin: Good point. I'll add tests for dataclass + pydantic + a case where tool returns a string payload and ensure we don't over-eagerly deserialize.

Anya: Do we want to push a patch release or put this in next minor? Customer-impacting so patch is preferred.

Matt: Patch release. Patch branch and backport after PR. I'll follow up with release infra.

Jin: Opening PR now — https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/4399 — includes fix, tests, and docs snippet.

Anya: Nice, thanks. Can you post CI green + changelog here when ready and I'll update the onboarding sample in the internal cookbook.

ci-bot: PR 4399 — checks pending.

Jin: ci green, tests passing, merged to patch branch. Changelog entry: "Fix async tool_call structured output double-serialization bug; ensure dataclass/pydantic return_type works in async client."

Anya: Awesome, thanks everyone. Please close thread when the docs sample is live in prod.

Matt: Closing once docs redeploy done.
